summary: No, not as a reversal signal. On BTC, ETH and SOL, the bottom wick settings did no better than random candles on 4h and daily, and the 1h gain after a bottom wick shows at 20 candles only. The result that holds up runs the other way: after a top wick signal started on 1h or 4h, price kept rising more than after random candles, which makes it a poor short trigger.

verdicts.use: Shorting a long top wick (signal start, threshold 1)
verdicts.text: Worse than random on 1h and 4h, at 10, 20, 50 and 100 candles, and still worse without its strongest stretch. Price kept rising after these wicks.

verdicts.use: Going long on a long bottom wick (signal start, threshold 1)
verdicts.text: Beat random on 1h at 20 candles only, and these signals fire mostly in volatile candles. Price moved more after them in a window that rose, which is timing, not direction.
Inside the luck band on 1h and 4h. On daily there are too few episodes to judge.

verdicts.use: Staying long while a bottom wick level holds (threshold 2, 200 bars)
verdicts.text: No better than random entries on 1h or 4h. On daily there are too few episodes to judge.

verdicts.use: Staying short while a top wick level holds (threshold 2, 200 bars)
verdicts.text: Worse than random on 1h, where price kept rising. On 4h it is inside the luck band, and on daily there are too few episodes.

notes: Shorting at the start of a top wick signal on 1h gave 1,493 entries in 1,159 separate moves. Twenty candles later they were 0.6% worse than random entries. On 4h the gap was 2.25%. Both hold without their strongest stretch and at 10, 20, 50 and 100 candles.

The top wick result shows on each coin on 1h. On 4h, BTC was 1.34% worse and SOL 4.36% worse, while ETH stayed inside the luck band. On 1h it was worse in uptrends and in downtrends, but in downtrends only at 10 and 20 candles. On 4h it was 2.11% worse in uptrends and showed nothing in downtrends. These signals fire mostly in volatile candles, so part of the gap may come from when they fire in a rising window.

Going long at the start of a bottom wick signal on 1h beat random entries by 0.31% after 20 candles. At 10, 50 and 100 candles it was inside the luck band. These signals fire mostly in volatile candles. Price moved more after them in a window that rose, and that is not a directional edge. SOL carries the result, at 1.07% above random. BTC was 0.2% worse, but only because of signals on Jun 12–15, 2022, during the Celsius withdrawal freeze. ETH showed nothing.

The same 1h bottom wick split by regime: 0.34% above random in uptrends, nothing in downtrends. On 4h the pooled result sat inside the luck band because the regimes cancel out. In uptrends it was 1.23% above random at every horizon. In downtrends it was 1.75% worse, but only because of signals on Nov 7–9, 2022, during the FTX collapse. Without them it is chance. The volatility timing applies here too.

Threshold 2 makes the bottom wick signal fire about one fifth as often on 1h, and it lands inside the luck band on 1h and 4h. The level version of the bottom wick, held for 200 bars, gave 37,418 entries in only 286 separate moves on 1h and showed nothing on 1h or 4h. The top wick level version was 0.34% worse than random on 1h, and that holds without its strongest stretch on Feb 19–23, 2021. On daily every setting has too few episodes or sits inside the luck band.

The usable shape is a negative one. A top wick signal on 1h or 4h is a reason to leave it out of a short bot's start condition, since price tended to keep rising after it. For a long DCA bot, a bottom wick start adds little on BTC and ETH, and the DCA orders and take profit do the work. If you add it as a filter beside an uptrend condition, expect it to fail in downtrend crashes, where bottom wicks marked the start of further falls.
